title: A fair invitation beyond silent accounting

captions.physics: Agreeing terms for a shared pleasure
captions.energy: Withdrawing before an invitation is voiced

meaning: Shared leisure becomes freer when fair agreement includes voiced wishes and private quiet does not turn into mutual accounting.
text: Agreeing on leisure can be easier than suggesting it in time. Justice in the physical position of Svadhisthana helps clarify conditions: time, format and room for both people’s choice. The Hermit in energy leans towards withdrawing and leaving a wish unnamed. Justice in emotions assesses whether initiative and participation are fairly shared. Her repeated appearance distinguishes an action from its inward response. Without a voiced invitation, fairness risks counting something you have not discussed and about which each is still only guessing.

For example, both would like a short walk, but each waits for the other’s suggestion. Later comes the thought: why must I organise it again? **Fair participation begins with a clear invitation rather than an unspoken account.** You can name the wish and discuss which outing suits both today. Refusing, postponing or offering another option remains possible. Neither has to guess what part of a pleasant evening they already owe without an expressed agreement.

The difficulty is defending equality by withholding initiative. You await an approach and feel the lack of shared time more sharply while your own wish stays hidden. Leisure is assessed before receiving a chance to happen. Solitude helps when it returns clear understanding you can share. A spoken preference gives material for fair choice without making an invitation an obligation to agree immediately for balance’s sake.
